title: Remove reliance on obsolete browser token binding
goal: Remove abandoned RFC 8471 token-binding observation when modernizing authentication middleware, while preserving HTTPS enforcement, cookie authentication and the application's authorization policy.

selectionNotes: Remove only an optional RFC 8471 observation after establishing that it is not part of the application's authentication decision. Do not turn a required binding check into unconditional acceptance.
TLS Token Binding (RFC 8471) is distinct from RFC 5929 channel binding. This recipe implements no replacement device binding, proof of possession, relay defense or token theft mitigation.
Kestrel's absent feature is observed on actual .NET10 HTTPS requests. Authentication, curator role authorization and HTTPS enforcement remain effective on both targets.

The sample mints real protected cookies inside the isolated test harness, not through a public login endpoint. Production sign-in and keys remain application-owned. Temporary certificate validation matches only the exact test certificate; no trust store changes.

evidence.scope: Actual Kestrel HTTPS with absent ITlsTokenBindingFeature and optional historical telemetry; real protected curator/visitor/invalid/absent cookies, exact 200/403/401 outcomes, HTTP400 and denied-handler exclusion. Audited reference identities and compiler/runtime hashes; no browser token-binding implementation.

Actual same authorization/HTTPS outcomes after removing feature lookup; isolated historical-source recompilation emits ASPDEPR010 on real RC2 references. No replacement protocol, production sign-in, channel-binding, browser or GA proof.
